source: graph_timing in the packet29 restore receipt: every captured graph replayed 20 times with a host sync, on the real checkpoint blocks

correction.earlier_claim: blocks are 61% of the sampler and 39% is not blocks
correction.earlier_method: scaled a synthetic 48-block chain (102.8 ms) by the weight ratio
correction.why_it_was_wrong: the synthetic block is 2.14 ms while the real block is 2.744 ms at the same token count, 28% cheaper, so it understated the blocks
correction.corrected: blocks are 81.5% of the sampler; only 18.5% is orchestration plus the non-block forward

weight_vs_activation.method: stage 2 has 4x the video tokens and identical weights, so the difference isolates the token-dependent work; assuming it scales linearly with tokens
weight_vs_activation.reading: The weight-reading part of the blocks achieves only about 59% of the measured copy roofline. That, not elementwise work, is the dominant remaining inefficiency -- and it is consistent with the block holding many small projections: an isolated audio q/k/v triple runs at 186 GB/s against 537.

consequence: Extending graph capture to whole contiguous runs is worth far less than estimated: the non-block share is 0.357 s, and capture would only remove part of it.
The remaining prize is inside the blocks. Lifting the weight-bound part from 59% to 90% of roofline would save roughly 0.45 s, which is the difference between missing and reaching the goal.
Fusing the three qualifying q/k/v sites is a down payment on exactly that mechanism, worth about 0.1 s.
